field_summary:
WASHINGTON, March 28, 2025 – Cargill Kitchen Solutions, a company in Lake Odessa, Michigan, is recalling approximately 212,268 pounds of liquid egg products that may contain a cleaning solution with sodium hypochlorite, announced the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) today. 

The liquid egg products were produced on March 12 and 13, 2025. The following items are subject to recall: [View the Labels]:

  • Caja de 32 oz. (2 lb.) que contiene “egg beaters ORIGINAL LIQUID EGG SUBSTITUTE” and date of "USAR ANTES DEL" 10 AGO 2025.
  • Caja de 32 oz. (2 lb.) that contains “egg beaters CAGE-FREE ORIGINAL LIQUID EGG SUBSTITUTE” and date of "USAR ANTES DEL" 09 AGO 2025.
  • Caja de 32 oz. (2 lb.) que contiene “egg beaters CAGE-FREE ORIGINAL FROZEN EGG SUBSTITUTE” and date of "USAR ANTES DEL" 07 AGO 2026.
  • Caja de 32 oz. (2 lb.) that contains “Bob Evans Better’n Eggs Made with Real Egg Whites” and date of "USAR ANTES DEL" 10 AGO 2025.

The recalled product is marked with the establishment number 'G'1804' printed in ink on the box. These products were shipped to distributors in Ohio and Texas for use in food service establishments in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, and Iowa. There may have been distribution at a national level.

The issue was discovered when FSIS received information about potential contamination of these products. After conducting an investigation and thorough evaluation of the cleaning solution contents, FSIS scientists concluded that use of this product is not expected to cause adverse health effects or insignificant risk, thus it is being recalled as Class III.

While FSIS does not expect adverse health effects from Class III recalls and there have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products, anyone with concerns about illness should contact a healthcare provider. 

FSIS is concerned that some of the product may be in consumers' refrigerators or food service establishments' freezers. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them and food service establishments not to serve them. These products should be discarded or returned to the point of sale.

FSIS routinely conducts follow-up inspections for effectiveness of recalls to verify that companies notify their customers and take necessary steps to ensure the product is no longer accessible to consumers.

Consumers and media with questions about this recall can contact Chuck Miller, Cargill Kitchen Solutions, at 1-844-419-1574 or media@cargill.com.

Consumers with food safety concerns may call the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or email questions to MPHotline@usda.gov. Consumers needing to report a problem with meat, poultry, or egg products can access the Electronic Consumer Complaint System 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
